  • Method Details

    • parseRadix

      public static int parseRadix(String number) throws NumberFormatException
      Parses an integer written in assembler-style notation.

      Accepted syntax (case-insensitive, no surrounding whitespace): optional sign +/-, followed by

      • 0x prefix: hexadecimal (0x1F)
      • h suffix: hexadecimal (1Fh)
      • b suffix or 0b prefix: binary (101b, 0b101)
      • o or q suffix: octal (17o, 17q)
      • d suffix or no affix: decimal (12d, 12; leading zeros are decimal too)
      The result must fit into a signed 32-bit integer.
      Parameters:
      number - the number text
      Returns:
      parsed value
      Throws:
      NumberFormatException - if the text is not a number in a recognized format, or it overflows

    • formatHex

      public static String formatHex(int value, int digits)
      Formats a value as an uppercase hexadecimal number, left-padded with zeros.

      The result is never truncated: if the value needs more digits, all are emitted (negative values have 8 digits).

      Parameters:
      value - the value
      digits - minimal number of digits (e.g. 2 for a byte, 4 for a word, 8 for a dword)
      Returns:
      hexadecimal string without prefix or suffix

    • formatBinary

      public static String formatBinary(int value, int bits)
      Formats a value as a binary number, left-padded with zeros.

      The result is never truncated: if the value needs more bits, all are emitted (negative values have 32 bits).

      Parameters:
      value - the value
      bits - minimal number of bits
      Returns:
      binary string without prefix or suffix

    • formatBinary

      public static String formatBinary(int value, int bits, int groupBits)
      Formats a value as a binary number, left-padded with zeros, with bit groups separated by a space.

      Groups are counted from the least significant bit, e.g. formatBinary(0x2F, 10, 4) is "00 0010 1111". The result is never truncated (negative values have 32 bits).

      Parameters:
      value - the value
      bits - minimal number of bits
      groupBits - number of bits in a space-separated group; if <= 0, bits are not grouped
      Returns:
      binary string without prefix or suffix
